cls: Vaccine (oral cholera vaccine - killed whole-cell, with or without recombinant B subunit, or live attenuated)
pharm: Oral cholera vaccine that stimulates intestinal mucosal (secretory IgA) and systemic immunity against Vibrio cholerae O1 (and O139 in some products), reducing the risk of symptomatic cholera.
quick: Killed OCV: 2 oral doses 1-6 weeks apart; live attenuated (Vaxchora): single oral dose
Avoid food/drink for ~1 hour before and after each oral dose
Use if clearly needed; per public-health guidance (limited data)
Generally considered compatible per public-health guidance
Observe for hypersensitivity; ensure full schedule for protection
summary: Cholera vaccines are oral vaccines that protect against cholera caused by Vibrio cholerae. The killed whole-cell vaccines (e.g., Dukoral with recombinant B subunit, and Shanchol/Euvichol/mORCVAX without B subunit) are given as two doses, while the live attenuated single-dose vaccine (Vaxchora, CVD 103-HgR) protects adult travelers against V. cholerae O1. They induce gut mucosal and systemic immunity, reducing the risk of symptomatic cholera. They are generally well tolerated, with mild gastrointestinal symptoms most common. Killed oral cholera vaccines are WHO-prequalified and widely used in endemic settings; Vaxchora is FDA-approved for adult travelers (see pearls).
indications: Active immunization against cholera caused by Vibrio cholerae serogroup O1 (and O139 with some killed vaccines)
Prevention of cholera in travelers to endemic/epidemic areas and in populations during cholera outbreaks (killed oral cholera vaccines)
Vaxchora (live attenuated): prevention of cholera caused by V. cholerae serogroup O1 in adults traveling to cholera-affected areas

dosage.c: Killed OCV with B subunit (Dukoral) - adults and children >=6 years
dosage.d: 2 doses given 1-6 weeks apart; each dose with buffer in water

dosage.c: Killed OCV with B subunit (Dukoral) - children 2 to 5 years
Killed OCV without B subunit (Shanchol/Euvichol) - >=1 year
dosage.d: 2 doses given at least 14 days apart

dosage.c: Live attenuated (Vaxchora, CVD 103-HgR) - adults 18-64 years (and per label children/adolescents)
dosage.d: Single oral dose reconstituted with buffer, taken at least 10 days before potential exposure

admin: Administer orally only; do not inject
For killed vaccines (e.g., Dukoral), dissolve the supplied buffer granules in water and add the vaccine; drink within ~2 hours of preparation
For the live attenuated vaccine, reconstitute with the supplied buffer and drink within ~15 minutes; do not take with food
Avoid food and drink for about 1 hour before and after each dose
Separate oral typhoid vaccine and certain oral antibiotics/antimalarials from the live attenuated cholera vaccine per the product label
moa: Oral cholera vaccines deliver killed whole Vibrio cholerae bacteria (and, in some products, recombinant cholera toxin B subunit) or a live attenuated strain directly to the intestinal mucosa. This stimulates a local mucosal immune response, chiefly secretory IgA antibodies against the bacterial lipopolysaccharide and, where present, against cholera toxin (the B subunit is structurally similar to the heat-labile toxin of enterotoxigenic E. coli, giving some cross-protection). The resulting intestinal and systemic immunity inhibits bacterial colonization and toxin binding, reducing the incidence and severity of cholera.

absolute: Known severe hypersensitivity to the vaccine, any component, or to a previous dose
For the live attenuated vaccine: avoid in immunocompromised individuals (per label)
relative: Acute gastrointestinal illness or acute febrile illness (defer)
Immunodeficiency or immunosuppressive therapy (reduced response; live vaccine cautions)
Recent or concurrent oral antibiotics (may reduce live vaccine effectiveness)
monitor: Completion of the dosing schedule for adequate protection

preg: There are limited data on cholera vaccines in pregnancy. Killed oral cholera vaccines may be used during pregnancy when the risk of cholera is high, per public-health guidance. For the live attenuated vaccine, use in pregnancy only if clearly needed; data are limited.
lact: Cholera vaccines are generally considered compatible with breastfeeding; killed oral cholera vaccines may be given to breastfeeding women when indicated, per public-health guidance.
renal: No dose adjustment is required in renal impairment.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required in hepatic impairment.

moderate: Oral antibiotics - may interfere with the live attenuated vaccine; avoid antibiotics within ~14 days before to a few days after the live vaccine
Chloroquine and certain antimalarials - may reduce the immune response to the live attenuated vaccine; separate per label
Immunosuppressive therapy - may reduce vaccine immunogenicity
minor: Oral typhoid vaccine - separate administration from live cholera vaccine per label
interactions.food: Avoid food and drink for about 1 hour before and after each oral dose; food/buffer timing affects vaccine survival in the stomach.
interactions.diagnostics: No significant interference with laboratory tests.

monitoring: Observe for immediate hypersensitivity after administration
Confirm completion of the full dosing schedule and timing relative to travel
Counsel that protection is not immediate and is not absolute
counsel: Take the vaccine by mouth exactly as directed; complete all doses for protection
Avoid food and drink for about 1 hour before and after each dose
Mild stomach upset, cramps, or loose stools can occur and usually settle quickly
The vaccine does not give complete protection - continue safe food and water practices and good hygiene
Tell your provider about any antibiotics or other vaccines, and complete the course at least 1-2 weeks before travel
pk: Protective immunity develops about 1 week after completing the schedule (at least ~10 days before exposure for the live vaccine)
Mucosal/systemic antibody responses develop over the days to weeks after dosing
Protection lasts roughly 6 months to 2-3 years depending on product and age; boosters recommended
Store at 2-8 C; do not freeze; protect from light per the product label
pearls: Killed oral cholera vaccines (Dukoral, Shanchol, Euvichol) are WHO-prequalified and used widely in endemic areas and outbreaks; the live attenuated single-dose vaccine (Vaxchora) is FDA-approved for adult travelers
Killed vaccines need two (or three in young children) doses; the live attenuated vaccine is a single dose taken at least 10 days before travel
Avoid food/drink ~1 hour before and after each dose, and separate the live vaccine from oral antibiotics and certain antimalarials
Dukoral's recombinant B subunit gives short-term cross-protection against enterotoxigenic E. coli (traveler's diarrhea)
Protection is partial - emphasize safe water/food and hygiene; guidance based on WHO and manufacturer information
missed: If a dose in a multi-dose schedule is delayed beyond the recommended interval, complete the course as soon as possible; there is usually no need to restart, but follow the specific product label and public-health guidance. Ensure the schedule is finished before travel for adequate protection.
overdose: Overdose is not expected with oral cholera vaccines. Inadvertent administration of an extra dose may cause increased gastrointestinal symptoms; manage with supportive care.
